opening.headline: Project, GPT, Gem, and Notebook all deal with knowledge, and the differences are identified by matching components.
body: The ChatGPT project and GPT, the Claude project, Gemini's Gem, and Gemini Notebook all cover files and instructions. Teams are repeatedly asked which one to use. Although the names are different, they seem like completely different products, but when you open the screen, you can see that they have something in common: an instruction section and a data section.

In this lesson, we pair knowledge space products from three companies into the following components: guidance, knowledge, and sharing. While Project and Gem are guideline-oriented workspaces, Gemini Notebook is a source-oriented research tool. At the end, we discuss examples of choosing the right structure for the research team and sales team.

As of 2026-10: Gems are transitioning to skills. Personal accounts will be converted after November 2026, and Workspace business accounts will be converted after March 2027. The Gems screen below is based on the pre-migration environment. After moving the instructions and files, please check again for sharing and tool operation.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the components of the three companies' knowledge space products
Instructions, knowledge, and sharing functions for each product can be matched to each other.

screens.title: Project, GPT, Gem, and Notebook all deal with knowledge. What's the difference?
screens.lead:
First, we'll look at questions that frequently come up from our teams. Think about what labels your products have in common.

As of 2026-10: Gems are transitioning to skills. Personal accounts will be converted after November 2026, and Workspace business accounts will be converted after March 2027. The Gems screen below is based on the pre-migration environment. After moving the instructions and files, please check again for sharing and tool operation.

visual.alt: Four product name cards are laid out in a row, all with the same tag.

paragraphs: The ChatGPT project, GPT, Claude Project, Gemini's Gem, and Gemini Notebook all cover files and instructions. Teams are repeatedly asked which one to use.

Because the names are different, they seem like completely different products. However, when you open the screen, you can see something in common: there is an instruction section and a data section. If you can't distinguish between uses, the same data will be scattered in four places, and no one will know which one is the most up-to-date.
The question for this class is this. How do the structures of knowledge spaces with different names correspond?

screens.outro: First, let's think about the products you have used.

screens.title: Which knowledge space products have you used?
screens.lead: When you select each product icon, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You will not enter or submit your answer, so think first before clicking.

items.prompt: If you've used the ChatGPT project or GPT, where are the instructions, resources, and sharing?
items.answer: In a project, there are instructions in Project settings in the Overview menu, files in the Source area, and Shares in the Share menu. In GPT, instructions are located in the Instructions section of the builder and files are located in Knowledge. Keep in mind that there are separate places for rules and materials.

items.prompt: What was it like if you used the Claude project?
items.answer: On the project screen, write down the instructions using Set project instructions and upload the materials to the knowledge area on the right. Sharing is done using the Share project button in Team and Enterprise plans. The three positions are divided in the same way: guidance, resources, and sharing.

items.prompt: If you've used Gem or Gemini Notebook, what was it like?
items.answer: Gem writes down your name and instructions and uploads the file to Knowledge. Gemini Notebook posts material in the source panel and asks questions in chat. Although the names of the positions are different, you can find the rules, materials, and writing together everywhere.

screens.outro: Now that we know that the three positions are everywhere, let's start by looking at projects and gems.

screens.title: Projects and Gems: A Guide-Driven Workplace
screens.lead: Select each tab to see the components and sharing methods for each product. Notice how projects and gems differ.

visual.alt: A side-by-side illustration of the project on the left and the Gem card on the right, with each instruction and knowledge section.

tabs.label: ChatGPT Project
tabs.body: A project is a workspace that gathers related chats, files, and instructions in one place to keep you on the same page. Project guidelines apply only within that project and take precedence over global custom guidelines. When sharing, open the sharing window with Share, invite people or groups, and give them chat or editing permissions. Edit permissions allow you to edit instructions, upload or delete files, and invite others, while chat permissions allow you to view and interact with chat, files, and instructions, but cannot invite them.

tabs.label: Claude Project
tabs.body: The Claude Project is an independent workspace with its own chat history and knowledge. There are separate knowledge and guidelines, and the guidelines are used in all chats in the project. Team and Enterprise plans allow you to share projects with other members of your organization, with View permissions allowing you to view and chat with content but not editing it, and Edit permissions allowing you to edit instructions and knowledge and manage members. Your administrator may have turned off project sharing.

tabs.label: Gemini Gem
tabs.body: Gem is a custom assistant that you create by giving it a name and instructions and uploading it to Knowledge. Files can be uploaded from your device or added from Drive, and knowledge citations can be turned off in settings. The point is that Gem is an assistant with one role. Gems created in the Gemini web app also appear in the mobile app and in the Gemini side panel in Google Workspace.

tabs.label: Difference between Project and Gem
tabs.body: The difference is that a project is a space that bundles multiple chats, and a gem is an assistant with a single role. A project is suitable for carrying out multiple tasks within the same context, and a gem is suitable for performing one set role repeatedly. Both products have the same structure in that they are divided into instructions and knowledge sections.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the instruction-centric space, let's take a look at the source-centric Gemini Notebook.

screens.title: Gemini Notebook: A source-driven knowledge space
screens.lead: Select a number marker to see a detailed description of each area of the Gemini Notebook screen. Start by clicking on the Source panel one by one.

visual.alt: A screen with Gemini Notebook's source panel, chat panel, and Studio panel laid out horizontally.

markers.label: source panel
markers.title: Source: Notebook Evidence
markers.body: Gemini Notebook is a research tool where you post sources and receive answers with citations based on those sources. Previous name: NotebookLM. In the Sources panel, add or deselect sources to determine what you want to base your work on. Each source is provided with a maximum of 500,000 words or a 200MB upload file.

markers.label: chat panel
markers.title: Chat: Source-based questions and answers
markers.body: The chat panel generates a summary of the entire source and allows you to ask questions or give instructions about the source. Answers are based solely on notebook sources and are accompanied by citations to identify which sources they came from. Notebooks can also have custom instructions.

markers.label: Studio panel
markers.title: Studio: Deliverables from source
markers.body: The Studio panel allows you to create and view output based on your source code. Things like reports, audio outlines, mind maps, and slides. This feature can only be used in Gemini Notebook, and the output of the Studio panel cannot be created in the Gemini app.

markers.label: independence
markers.title: notebooks are independent of each other
markers.body: A notebook is a collection of source code for a specific project, and each notebook is independent of the others. Gemini Notebook cannot refer to information from multiple notebooks at once. Therefore, it is basic to create one notebook per topic.

markers.label: Gemini app integration
markers.title: notebook visible in Gemini app
markers.body: Notebooks created in Gemini Notebook also appear in the Gemini app's navigation, and their names, sources, and instructions are synchronized in both. However, the basis for the answer is different. Gemini Notebook is based solely on the notebook source, while the Gemini App is based on the notebook source but may add web search and other tools.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the four areas, let's put the components of the four products in one table and match them.

screens.title: Component correspondence table of knowledge space
screens.lead: The table below maps the components of the four products into four rows: instructions, knowledge, sharing, and precautions. Read the same row horizontally to see where the same role is located even if the product name is different.

data.notes: Workspace administrators can turn Gemini Notebook usage on or off on a per-user basis. The location of sharing permissions and administrator settings varies depending on the product, so please check where they are set before introduction.

screens.outro: Now that you've read the correspondence table, let's explain the process of choosing a structure using a team example.

screens.title: Commentary: A knowledge space tailored to your research team
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow the process as the research team's needs are matched with product features one by one and the reasons for selection are accumulated.

steps.title: request
steps.body: The research team must check the evidence of dozens of papers and articles, along with citations, and create a summary report based on this. The key is that you need to be able to determine which source every answer came from.

steps.title: Product Selection: Gemini Notebook
steps.body: Gemini Notebook focuses on source-based cited answers and outputs such as reports and mind maps. This is appropriate because the request is to verify evidence and produce output. The project is centered around continuity of guidance and chat, so it is relatively less suited to evidence verification.

steps.title: Structure: One notebook per topic
steps.body: Notebooks are independent of each other and you cannot reference multiple notebooks at once. So, I divide it into one notebook per research topic. Mixing sources on unrelated topics in one notebook will cause citations and summaries to become blurred.

steps.title: Extension: Leveraging Notebooks in Gem
steps.body: You can add notebooks to Knowledge in Gem. So, you can paste the organized notebook into the knowledge of a Gem with a single role. It is a method that connects source-centered research and role-centered assistants.

steps.title: instructions
steps.body: The instructions are to cite the source and answer that there is no content that is not in the source. In research, it is more important to reveal groundlessness rather than plausible guesses. The instructions are shared between the notebook and the Gemini app, so they change no matter which side you edit them from.

screens.outro: Now that we've looked at a research-oriented case, let's now look at the case of a sales team.

screens.title: Commentary: A knowledge space for your sales team
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow the steps through Requirements, Configuration, Sharing Permissions, and Operational Attention.

steps.title: request
steps.body: Multiple sales reps need to share the same proposal tone, price list, and case materials to keep the conversation going. The key is that even if different people use the same rules and materials, they must be able to continue working from previous conversations.

steps.title: Product Selection: Project
steps.body: Projects are perfect for continuing work by keeping instructions, files, and previous chats together. If the tone of the proposal is placed in the guidelines, and the price list and case materials are placed in the knowledge base, the same rules and materials are used even if the person in charge is different. If you create a personal gem for each person, your tone and material will vary from person to person.

steps.title: Divide sharing rights
steps.body: Give editing rights to only two or three administrators, and leave the rest with chat or view rights. Anyone with editing permissions can modify instructions and upload or delete files, so the more you give, the greater the risk that your instructions and materials will be shaken.

steps.title: Check administrator settings
steps.body: If your organization uses Claude, make sure your administrator has control over project sharing settings. Claude allows the Owner to turn off project sharing for the organization, and once turned off, new shares cannot be added. ChatGPT may also have a limited invitation range depending on your workspace settings.

steps.title: Pricelist Review Connections
steps.body: For materials that change, such as price lists, the connection is reviewed rather than uploaded. The uploaded copy must be replaced every time it is revised, and if replacement is late, the old price will be announced. If you have a source you can link to, link to it to keep the sources together.

screens.outro: Now that we've solved the two cases, let's summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaways
screens.lead: Summarizes the contents of this class. As you read, try to answer the initial question: How do the structures of knowledge spaces with different names correspond?

paragraphs: The initial question was how the structures of knowledge spaces with different names correspond. Although they may have different names, these three components are present in any product: guidance, knowledge, and sharing. The instructions and sources of the ChatGPT project, the instructions and knowledge of the Claude project, the instructions and knowledge of the Gem, and the custom instructions and sources of the notebook correspond to each other.

Each product has a different focus. A project is a space for grouping multiple chats, a gem is an assistant with a single role, and a notebook is centered around cited answers and output based on sources. Notebooks are independent of each other, so you cannot reference multiple notebooks at once.
The location of sharing permissions and administrator settings also vary by product. Before adoption, check who edits, who only views, and where administrators control it.

The question from the first scene, which one to use, can now be answered. If rules and subsequent conversations are important, choose Project or Gem, and if checking evidence and output are important, choose Notebook. If both things are important, decide first which one is more important and then choose.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: Compare by components, not by product name. By pairing guidance, knowledge, and sharing, you can quickly get to know a product even if you're new to it.

glossary.def: A workspace that brings together related chat, files, and instructions in one place.
Gemini's custom assistant that you create with your name, instructions, and knowledge files.
It is a research tool that uploads sources and creates cited answers and output. Previous name: NotebookLM.
Even if the product name is different, the perspective is to pair and compare through instructions, knowledge, and sharing.

misconceptions.myth: If the name is different, the structure is also completely different.
misconceptions.fact: They can be paired with instruction boxes, knowledge boxes, and sharing settings. Just the central elements are different, but the components correspond.

misconceptions.myth: Notebook You can refer to multiple sources at once.
misconceptions.fact: Each notebook is independent of the others, and Gemini Notebook cannot reference multiple notebooks simultaneously.

misconceptions.myth: When you share it, it looks the same everywhere.
misconceptions.fact: Each product is different. Notebooks shared from Gemini Notebook are not visible in the Gemini app.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Although the names are different, the structure of guidance, knowledge, and sharing is the same.
A project is a place to group chats, a gem is a role, and a notebook is source-centric.
Notebooks are independent of each other and responses are source-based.
Check sharing permissions and administrator settings for each product.
